questions.question: Which LGE pattern is most characteristic of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM)?
choices: A. Subendocardial in the LAD territory
B. Patchy, mid-myocardial enhancement at the junction of the RV and LV (hinge points)
questions.detail: HCM typically features mid-wall enhancement, often at the interventricular septal insertion points.

questions.question: Global subendocardial LGE that does NOT follow a coronary territory is a classic sign of:
questions.detail: Amyloid features diffuse, global subendocardial enhancement and difficulty nulling the myocardium on LGE.

questions.question: Which non-ischemic cardiomyopathy presents with transient apical ballooning and a normal coronary angiogram?
questions.detail: Takotsubo involves apical dysfunction often triggered by emotional stress; notably, there is usually no LGE, unlike MI.

questions.question: A 25-year-old athlete presents with mid-wall and subepicardial LGE in the lateral wall. He has a recent history of a viral illness. What is the diagnosis?
questions.detail: Myocarditis characteristically shows subepicardial and mid-wall LGE, often in the lateral free wall.

questions.question: Which cardiomyopathy is associated with fatty replacement of the myocardium and an increased risk of VT in young patients?
questions.detail: ARVC features fibrofatty replacement of the RV wall and is a cause of sudden cardiac death.

questions.question: "Systolic anterior motion" (SAM) of the mitral valve is a common finding in:
questions.detail: SAM contributes to LV outflow tract obstruction in patients with septal hypertrophy.

questions.question: Cardiac sarcoidosis typically presents on CMR with which enhancement pattern?
choices: B. Patchy, multifocal mid-wall and subepicardial enhancement
D. Linear subendocardial in the RCA territory
questions.detail: Sarcoidosis is a 'mimic' but usually shows patchy non-ischemic enhancement and can involve the conduction system.

questions.question: Which radionuclide scan is most sensitive for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis (specifically the ATTR type)?
choices: B. Tc-99m MDP or PYP (bone scan agents)
questions.detail: ATTR amyloidosis shows intense myocardial uptake of bone-seeking radiopharmaceuticals.

questions.question: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized on CMR by:
choices: A. Markedly increased LV wall thickness
C. Increased LV volumes and a "mid-wall" linear LGE pattern (in some cases)
questions.detail: DCM features ventricular dilation and reduced EF; mid-wall enhancement may be seen in about 30% of idiopathic cases.

questions.question: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, classically leads to which cardiac MRI finding?
choices: C. LV apical aneurysm and LGE
questions.detail: An apical aneurysm is a characteristic late complication of Chagasic cardiomyopathy.

questions.question: "Loeffler endocarditis" is a restrictive cardiomyopathy associated with:
questions.detail: Loeffler disease causes endocardial fibrosis and thrombus formation due to eosinophilic infiltration.

questions.question: Iron overload cardiomyopathy (hemochromatosis) is best quantified on MRI using:
questions.detail: Excess iron causes reduced T2* signal; a T2* <20 ms indicates myocardial iron overload.

questions.question: "Non-compaction" cardiomyopathy is diagnosed when the ratio of non-compacted to compacted myocardium is:
questions.detail: A ratio of > 2.3 in end-diastole is the standard CMR criterion for non-compaction.

questions.question: Which imaging modality is "first-line" for evaluating most non-ischemic cardiomyopathies?
questions.detail: While CMR is more accurate, echo is the initial tool for evaluating function, wall thickness, and valves.

questions.question: In cardiac sarcoidosis, FDG-PET/CT is used to identify:
choices: B. Areas of active inflammatory granulomatous disease
questions.detail: Active sarcoid granulomas are FDG-avid, helping guide therapy and monitor response.
